transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~68 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Samira Khan, Tom Briggs, Leah Ortiz, Miguel Santos (Redwood) / Priya Raman, Evan Cole, Rosa Chen, Ben Harper (Synthesis Labs)
Artifacts referenced: perf-spreadsheet.xlsx (link), kernel-profiling-notes.md (will share), slides: GPU-runtime-deep-dive.pdf

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick intro, i'm jordan, account lead, with samira and tom from platform and runtime.  todays a deep dive into kernel selection and cudagraphs behavior 
[00:18] Priya Raman: thanks jordan. we wanted a session that dives into why we're seeing jitter on p99 with our 16B model and where tensorRT-LLM vs vLLM differ, especially when we enable cudagraphs.
[00:30] Samira Khan: great, that's exactly what we prepared. quick agenda: kernel selection heuristics, cudagraphs warmup behavior, KV cache strategy for long context, batching tradeoffs, then quantization notes. we'll surface tooling to reproduce traces.
[00:45] Evan Cole: small ask - we run on a 4xA100 on-prem cluster behind a strict VPC and we have an H100 pilot next quarter. looking for a reproducible benchmark and guidance for fallback strategies if quantized runs degrade quality.
[01:02] Tom Briggs: noted. from infra perspective, we care about deterministic cudagraphs (warm start) and how kernel selection changes for 1-shot vs streaming token generation.

[05:10] Samira: starting with kernel selection - our runtime profiles ops and picks kernels based on seq len, head dims, and hardware. in practice TRT-LLM (TensorRT-LLM) often picks fused attention kernels on H100 that beat default cuda kernels; vLLM path tends to use aten/cutlass for certain sizes which can be better at small batch / low latency.
[05:37] Ben Harper: can you expand on the cases where TRT wins vs vLLM? we've seen TRT faster for generation but occasional latency spikes.
[05:50] Samira: yes - TRT fused kernels give throughput wins when the kernel fits resources and cuFFT-like memory is stable. the spikes usually correlate with cudagraph replays or kernel fallback when a new sequence length triggers a different kernel path. if cudagraphs are recompiled at runtime because of dynamic dims, you can see micro-pauses.
[06:20] Rosa Chen: we observed cudagraphs warmup for first few requests, then it gets steady. is there a recommended warmup pattern?
[06:32] Samira: recommended: deterministic sequence of warmup prompts to prime KV cache and cudagraphs, plus keep-alive traffic for a short TTL. we ship examples: warmup N=20 sequences with varying lengths to avoid recompilation during real traffic. also avoid dynamic batching that changes key dims during warmup.

[12:15] Priya: what about KV cache prefetching? for long context chat our prefix cache hits are sometimes low and we see repeated recomputation.
[12:30] Samira: two levers: prefix chunking and eager KV prefetch. prefix chunking divides the prompt into cacheable segments; eager prefetch requests the KV blocks before generation starts. tradeoff is memory. in our runtime we keep a sliding window and evict LRU; on constrained GPUs you may need to increase local NVMe swap or use host staging.

[18:05] Evan: quantization - we've tried 4-bit and saw 8-10% quality drop on some evals. is that expected? any rollbacks?
[18:22] Samira: quality regressions depend on model and calibration. for many Llama-family variants, 4-bit with per-channel quant and activation clipping retains quality, but you'll need eval sets. rollback: we recommend A/B deploy with canary routing and automatic fallback to fp16 if per-request evals cross threshold. Tom: we can talk about how to wire the rollout.

[22:40] Tom Briggs: on networking/VPC - deployment in your VPC means we can do a private control plane, customer-managed peering. egress is minimized; logs and metrics delivered to your logging endpoint. Rosa asked about firewall ports: we need outbound 443 to the control plane and a small mTLS port for agent.
[23:05] Rosa Chen: ok we'll check with infra, expect some delays on strict change windows.

[28:00] Samira: back to cudagraphs - when cudagraphs are stable you get huge CPU offload and consistent latency. caveat: cudagraphs are deterministic only when shapes are constant. dynamic prompt lengths or tokenization changes can force recompile. we recommend a single cudagraph per model shape used by inference (e.g., seq_len 512 and seq_len 2048) and route requests to the matching executor.
[30:12] Ben Harper: is there a cost to maintaining multiple compiled graphs? memory pressure?
[30:25] Samira: yes compiled graphs hold device memory for kernels and temporaries; plan for ~10-20% overhead per extra compiled graph depending on model. that's where smart routing helps - small latency-sensitive requests go to a low-latency executor with smaller graph, heavy batched throughput goes to a separate pool.

[35:40] Priya: about TRT-LLM vs vLLM again - we saw vLLM more stable when running many small concurrent streams. is that something you've seen?
[35:52] Samira: absolutely. vLLM's scheduling is optimized for small token-by-token workloads and dynamic batching; TRT tends to shine on larger contiguous workloads. our runtime can route by concurrency profile: if qps per connection is low, prefer vLLM or cutlass kernels; if a heavy batched job, prefer TRT fused kernels.

[41:10] Evan: measuring perf - what traces should we send? we'd prefer a minimal set to reproduce p99 spikes.
[41:25] Samira: send: nvprof/cupti traces around spike windows, rt logs (kernel fallback events), cudagraph replay logs, and sample prompts. we have a tracing script samira/profile_cudagraphs.sh - i'll attach. also we want raw scheduler logs and a perf-spreadsheet template.

[47:00] Jordan Lee: quick pricing note - if you want dedicated pools for the pilot we can surface reserved pricing; tom will follow up with throughput tiers.
[47:18] Tom Briggs: yes i'll draft reserved capacity options - we'll highlight throughput (tokens/sec) for 16B and 70B models.

[53:30] Rosa Chen: about quantized rollback strategy - how fast is fallback to fp16 if quality monitor reports regressions?
[53:45] Samira: we can do traffic-level canary with metrics; fallback window can be minutes depending on how you configure your rollout. for strict RL, choose aggressive thresholds and automatic fallback to fp16 executor. we also log diffs for sample prompts to help root cause.

[59:10] Ben Harper: any gotchas when migrating from A100 to H100? i've seen different kernel preferences and memory alloc patterns.
[59:22] Samira: H100 changes memory allocator behavior and offers better FP16/FP8 fused kernels; TRT often gets bigger wins on H100. biggest gotcha: different graph compilation times and sometimes larger temporary buffers - so plan benchmark on target hardware. also check cuDNN/driver versions.

[63:40] Jordan Lee: recap and next steps: we'll share kernel profiling notes, the cudagraphs tracing script, and the perf spreadsheet. Synthesis to provide access window for on-prem benchmark. Tom will share Dedicated pricing. schedule pilot kickoff for week of Dec 14.
[64:05] Priya Raman: thanks everyone, this was useful - we'll get Rosa and Miguel to coordinate windows and infra.
[64:20] Jordan Lee: thanks, i'll follow up with notes and links.
[64:25] Meeting end.
